theorem_title: A uniform residue-20 tail for every root congruent to eleven modulo twenty-seven
natural_language_statement:
Let $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be the shortcut Collatz map: $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$. Write $T^k$ for its $k$-fold iterate, with $T^0(n)=n$.

Let $z\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $z\equiv11\pmod{27}$. Then

$$
\exists m,b\in\mathbb N,\quad m>0,\quad m\equiv20\pmod{27},\quad T^b(m)=z,\quad m\le64z.
$$

This gives a bounded-size ancestor; strict descent relative to the later original root requires a separate power comparison.

theorem CollatzWork.residueAncestor_refinedTail (z : Nat) (hz : z % 27 = 11) :
    ∃ m b : Nat, 0 < m ∧ m % 27 = 20 ∧
      shortcutIter b m = z ∧ m ≤ 64 * z := by sorry
